title: Palabras council candidate
description: One line of a council bundle's candidates.jsonl. The council CLI writes it; the C# importer validates it against this file before any database write. Field names are snake_case because the bundle is a data interchange format, not the app's camelCase API. Vocabulary that maps to a word column (pos, cefr, register, topic, key) reuses content/schema/word.schema.json so the importer never translates two dialects. Schema keywords stay inside the tools/content-lint/validate.js subset.

key.description: Stable word key, same shape as a content file id. Unique within one bundle.

lemma.description: Spanish headword with correct orthography. Maps to words.headword.

gender.description: words.gender vocabulary, not the design example's short 'f': one dialect for both sides of the contract.

topic.description: Primary review topic. A word may gain more topics later through the corpus; the bundle carries exactly one.

region.description: ES = peninsular-generic, ES-NA = Navarre-specific. The importer maps these codes to words.region_scope; the bundle never carries the scope word itself.

register.description: words.register vocabulary (the column has no CHECK). Alternative-level register is a narrower enum.

latam_equivalent.description: Latin-American equivalent the consultants name, kept for the lint report only. Never imported as content.

senses.description: One item = one sense, same rule as the content corpus: do not merge two meanings into one sense.

alternatives.description: Pre-generated reviewer chips. Per-sense counts are a semantic rule: 2-4 gloss, 1-3 example, 0-2 lemma/regional_variant/register_variant.

en_accepted.description: Defaults to the gloss split on comma-space when absent, exactly like the corpus importer.

es_accepted.description: Defaults to the lemma when absent.

field.description: Also written to word_alternatives.field, which is the column constrained to this vocabulary. The importer copies it into kind too (kind has no CHECK; the legacy reviewer-chip resolver understands both). The v1 kinds synonym/near-synonym/different-sense/regional/register are not valid here.

sense.description: Zero-based index into senses. Absent means 0.

support.description: Number of models that proposed this value. Must equal models.length; ranking is support desc.

models.description: Model ids that proposed the value. Every id must be declared in the manifest.

target_key.description: Existing word key this alternative points at. Must resolve inside the bundle or the caller-supplied known-key set; a dangling reference is refused because it would later break the undo path.

register.description: word_alternatives.register CHECK vocabulary; narrower than the word-level register enum.

run_id.description: Must equal manifest.run_id; the importer refuses a candidate from another run.

agreement.description: critique_ok / critique_succeeded. Band is derived from it and must agree.

band.description: alta >= 0.75, media 0.50-0.74. Below 0.50 the candidate belongs in dropped.jsonl, so it is not a valid band here.

proposal_support.description: Fraction of proposing models that produced this candidate (proposed_by.length / models_succeeded.propose). Tie-breaker only.

proposed_by.description: Model ids that proposed the winning candidate itself. Not the same set as alternatives[].models: those list the models behind a dissenting value. Every id must be declared in manifest.models and must have phases.propose "ok"; the importer writes one word_provenance row per id. Required, so a bundle produced before the field existed is refused instead of importing provenance inferred from alternatives.

lint_warnings.description: Surviving Peninsular-Spanish concerns. Shown to the reviewer as a red chip; never blocks import.

lint_actions.description: Audit of automatic lint fixes (for example swapping a LatAm primary for a clean alternative).

issues.description: Issue codes (register, regional, example, ...), not free text: they become word_provenance.issues.
